decisions.choice: crafty: shrewd, clever in a way that can serve good or bad ends
decisions.reason: The word can be praise, "prudent", as often in Proverbs (Proverbs 12:16, 23), or blame, "crafty" (Job 5:12). Here the serpent's cleverness is used to mislead. The word sounds like "naked" in the verse before (2:25): the man and woman are naked, the serpent is shrewd.

decisions.choice: the serpent: one of the animals God made, which speaks
decisions.reason: The serpent is described as one of the wild animals God made, and the text does not explain how it can speak or say who is behind it. Later scripture identifies "the ancient serpent" with the devil and Satan (Revelation 12:9; 20:2; compare John 8:44).

decisions.choice: did God really say: a question that twists the command
alternatives: a statement of surprise: so God has said ...!
decisions.reason: The words can be a question or an exclamation; either way they distort what God said. God allowed every tree but one (2:16-17); the serpent makes it sound as though he forbade them all. It also calls him only "God", not "the LORD God" as the narrator does.

decisions.choice: It (the serpent)
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no neuter, so the serpent is "he"; Balanced and Readable say "it", as English does for an animal. Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: snake
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word; "serpent" is the traditional one.

decisions.choice: el SEÑOR (default); Yahvé with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: The divine name: "el SEÑOR" by default, "Yahvé" with the setting, as set out at 2:4. The span takes in the article or contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé").

decisions.choice: la serpiente at every level
decisions.reason: English Readable says "snake" because "serpent" is old-fashioned; Spanish "serpiente" is both the traditional and the everyday word for a large snake, so every level keeps it. It is feminine, so the question of "he" or "it" (English r-en-1) does not arise; Spanish mostly leaves the subject unstated.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms for the plural "you" (3:1-5)
decisions.reason: The serpent speaks to the woman with plural verbs ("you will eat" is plural), and the woman answers with "we": the man is included, and he is there (verse 6). Spanish keeps the plural, which is a reader setting: ustedes forms (the default) or vosotros forms (as in Spain). This holds for the whole conversation, verses 1-5.

decisions.choice: el jardín
decisions.reason: "Huerto" is the traditional word in Spanish Bibles, but today it suggests a vegetable plot; "jardín" is the ordinary word for a planted garden and is the one Spanish speakers use for the garden of Eden.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced; passé composé at Readable
decisions.reason: The tense choice for French narrative in Genesis, recorded in 1:1: the passé simple of written narrative at Literal and Balanced ("il dit"), the passé composé of spoken French at Readable ("il a demandé"). Speech keeps the tenses of speech ("Dieu a dit").

decisions.choice: le serpent ... il, at every level; rusé (L), astucieux (B), malin et rusé (R)
decisions.reason: "Serpent" is both the traditional and the everyday French word, so Readable needs no change (English r-en-2), and French refers to the animal as "il" at every level, having no neuter (r-en-1). The adjective can be praise or blame (m1); "rusé" and "astucieux" carry the shrewdness that misleads here.

decisions.choice: nyoka ... mjanja (L, B); mwerevu na mjanja (R)
decisions.reason: "Mwerevu" is clever, usually as praise; "mjanja" is cunning, cleverness used to trick, which is how the serpent uses it (m1). Readable keeps both, as the English Readable says "clever and sly". "Nyoka" takes the animate agreement ("alikuwa", "akamwambia") at every level.

decisions.choice: the serpent says "các người" to the woman, and the woman "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: The serpent speaks to the woman as to an equal stranger, and its "you" is plural, taking in the man (m3); "các người" is the plain plural. The woman answers for both of them with "chúng tôi" (3:2).

decisions.choice: The serpent and the woman speak to each other in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew shows no rank between the serpent and the woman, and the terms note does not settle it; the plain style used between equals fits a conversation in which the serpent presumes to correct God. A reviewer may prefer the woman to speak more politely.

decisions.choice: a serpente (L, B), a cobra (R); "ela" at every level
decisions.reason: For chapter 3. "Serpente" and "cobra" are feminine in Portuguese, so the serpent is "ela" at every level, and the words that agree with it are feminine ("astuta", "maldita"). The English Literal keeps the Hebrew "he"; Portuguese cannot, and the feminine says nothing about the serpent's sex.

decisions.choice: vocês
decisions.reason: The serpent's verb is plural: it speaks to the woman as one of two, the man being there (3:6), so it says "vocês"; the woman answers with "nós" and quotes God's plural "vocês" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: you will not surely die: the serpent denies God's own words
decisions.reason: The serpent repeats God's exact form of words from 2:17, "dying you will die", with "not" placed in front. It does not only question God's word now; it contradicts it.

decisions.choice: Non, vous ne mourrez pas à coup sûr

decisions.reason: The serpent repeats God's words of 2:17 with "not" in front (m1). Literal keeps the same wording as 2:17 ("tu mourras à coup sûr") so that the reader can hear the echo, and puts "Non" first so that the denial is not read as "not certainly".

decisions.choice: Kufa hamtakufa
decisions.reason: The serpent repeats God's doubled verb of 2:17 ("kufa utakufa") with "not" added (m1). Literal keeps the same form, so that the echo is heard; Balanced says "Hamtakufa kamwe!" (you will never die).

decisions.choice: the speaker named before the words (B, R)
alternatives: after the words, as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Vietnamese names the speaker first and introduces the words with a colon; the serpent's speech then runs on into verse 5 with no new opening mark.

decisions.choice: like God
decisions.reason: The word for God has a plural form and can mean "gods" or heavenly beings, and the following word "knowing" is plural, which could favor "like gods". But the serpent has just used the same word for God himself, and 3:22 ("like one of us") ties the knowledge to God. The serpent offers what belongs to God.

decisions.choice: your eyes will be opened: you will see and understand what you did not before
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for coming to see what was hidden (21:19; 2 Kings 6:17). It does come true in verse 7, but what they see is not what the serpent promised: they see that they are naked.

decisions.choice: God knows: the serpent suggests that God is holding something back
decisions.reason: The serpent presents God's command as jealous: God forbids the tree because he knows it would make them like him. The half-truth is the danger: their eyes are opened (verse 7) and they do gain a knowledge God has (verse 22), but they also die, as God said.

decisions.choice: no "for" at the start
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new quotation, since they ended the serpent's first words in verse 4; the Hebrew "for" joins the two halves of one speech.

decisions.choice: conocedores del bien y del mal
alternatives: sabiendo el bien y el mal
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "knowing" is plural and goes with "you" (m1). A plural Spanish noun shows that the knowing is theirs while keeping "como Dios"; a gerund ("sabiendo") could be read as describing God. Balanced and Readable say it with a verb, "conoceréis".

decisions.choice: os olhos de vocês
decisions.reason: "Seus" could be read as "his" or "their"; "de vocês" makes plain that the serpent means the man's and the woman's eyes (style section 4).

records.literal_gloss: And saw the woman that good [was] the tree for food, and that a delight it [was] to the eyes, and desirable [was] the tree to make wise, and she took from its fruit and ate, and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

en.L: And the woman saw that the tree [was] good for food, and that it [was] a delight to the eyes, and the tree [was] desirable to make [one] wise, and she took from its fruit and ate, and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.
en.B: The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining wisdom. So she took some of its fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.
en.R: The woman saw that the fruit of the tree looked good to eat. It was beautiful, and she wanted the wisdom it would give her. So she picked some fruit and ate it. Her husband was with her, and she gave some to him, and he ate it too.

es.L: Y la mujer vio que el árbol [era] bueno como alimento, y que [era] un deleite para los ojos, y [que] el árbol [era] deseable para dar sabiduría; y tomó de su fruto y comió, y dio también a su marido, [que estaba] con ella, y él comió.
es.B: La mujer vio que el árbol era bueno para comer, que deleitaba la vista y que era deseable para obtener sabiduría. Así que tomó de su fruto y lo comió. Le dio también a su marido, que estaba con ella, y él también comió.
es.R: La mujer vio que la fruta del árbol se veía buena para comer. Era hermosa, y ella deseaba la sabiduría que le daría. Así que cortó algunas frutas y comió. Su esposo estaba con ella. Ella le dio también a él, y él también comió.

fr.L: Et la femme vit que l’arbre [était] bon pour la nourriture, et qu’il [était] un délice pour les yeux, et [que] l’arbre [était] désirable pour rendre sage ; et elle prit de son fruit et mangea, et elle en donna aussi à son mari [qui était] avec elle, et il mangea.
fr.B: La femme vit que l’arbre était bon pour se nourrir, qu’il était un délice pour les yeux et qu’il était désirable pour acquérir la sagesse. Elle prit donc de son fruit et en mangea. Elle en donna aussi à son mari, qui était avec elle, et il en mangea.
fr.R: La femme a vu que le fruit de l’arbre avait l’air bon à manger. Il était beau, et elle voulait la sagesse qu’il allait lui donner. Alors elle a cueilli du fruit et en a mangé. Son mari était avec elle ; elle lui en a donné, et il en a mangé lui aussi.

sw.L: Na mwanamke akaona kwamba mti [ulikuwa] mzuri kwa chakula, na kwamba [ulikuwa] wa kufurahisha macho, na mti [ulikuwa] wa kutamanika kwa kumpa mtu hekima; akachukua kutoka matunda yake akala, naye akatoa pia kwa mume wake [aliyekuwa] pamoja naye, na yeye akala.
sw.B: Mwanamke akaona kwamba mti huo ulikuwa mzuri kwa chakula, unapendeza macho, na unatamanika kwa kupata hekima. Basi akachuma baadhi ya matunda yake akala. Akampa pia mume wake, aliyekuwa hapo pamoja naye, naye akala.
sw.R: Mwanamke akaona kwamba matunda ya mti ule yalionekana mazuri kula. Yalikuwa mazuri kuyatazama, naye alitamani hekima ambayo yangempa. Basi akachuma matunda kadhaa akala. Mume wake alikuwa pamoja naye; akampa baadhi, naye akala pia.

vi.L: Và người nữ thấy rằng cây ấy [thì] tốt để làm thức ăn, và rằng nó [là] một vật đẹp mắt, và cây ấy [là] đáng ao ước để làm cho [người ta] khôn ngoan, và nàng hái trái của nó và ăn, và nàng cũng đưa cho chồng mình ở với mình, và người ăn.
vi.B: Người nữ thấy trái của cây ấy ăn ngon, đẹp mắt, và đáng ao ước để được khôn ngoan. Vậy nàng hái trái ấy mà ăn. Nàng cũng đưa cho chồng mình, là người đang ở với nàng, và người cũng ăn.
vi.R: Người phụ nữ thấy trái của cây ấy trông ăn rất ngon. Trái ấy rất đẹp, và nàng muốn có sự khôn ngoan mà trái ấy sẽ ban cho. Vậy nàng hái trái ấy và ăn. Chồng nàng đang ở với nàng, và nàng đưa cho chồng một ít, và người cũng ăn.

ko.L: 그리고 여자가 보니 그 나무는 먹기에 좋고, 그것은 눈에 즐거움이며, 그 나무는 [사람을] 지혜롭게 하기에 탐스러웠다. 그래서 여자가 그 열매를 따서 먹고, 자기와 함께 있는 자기 남편에게도 주니, 그도 먹었다.
ko.B: 여자가 보니 그 나무는 먹기에 좋고, 보기에 즐겁고, 지혜를 얻기에 탐스러웠다. 그래서 여자는 그 열매를 따서 먹었다. 그리고 함께 있던 남편에게도 주니, 남편도 먹었다.
ko.R: 여자가 보니 그 나무의 열매는 먹음직스러웠다. 보기에도 아름다웠고, 그 열매가 줄 지혜도 갖고 싶었다. 그래서 여자는 열매를 따서 먹었다. 남편이 함께 있었는데, 여자가 남편에게도 주니 남편도 먹었다.

pt.L: E a mulher viu que a árvore [era] boa para comer, e que ela [era] um deleite para os olhos, e a árvore [era] desejável para tornar [alguém] sábio, e ela tomou do seu fruto e comeu, e deu também ao marido dela, com ela, e ele comeu.
pt.B: A mulher viu que a árvore era boa para comer, uma delícia para os olhos e desejável para obter sabedoria. Então colheu um pouco do seu fruto e o comeu. Deu também ao seu marido, que estava com ela, e ele comeu.
pt.R: A mulher viu que a fruta da árvore parecia boa para comer. Era bonita, e ela queria a sabedoria que a fruta daria a ela. Então ela colheu algumas frutas e comeu. O marido dela estava com ela, e ela deu um pouco para ele, e ele também comeu.

decisions.choice: good for food, a delight to the eyes, desirable to make wise
decisions.reason: The three phrases describe how desire grows: the body, the eyes, the mind. The first two echo the trees God gave in 2:9, "pleasing to look at and good for food"; the third is what the serpent promised. 1 John 2:16 uses a similar three-part list.

decisions.choice: to make wise: to give insight, success
decisions.reason: The verb means to have or give insight and to act wisely and successfully. Some take it here as "to contemplate", but its usual sense, wisdom, fits the serpent's promise of knowledge.

decisions.choice: her husband with her: the man was there
alternatives: her husband, who joined her later
decisions.reason: "With her" places the man at the scene. He says nothing during the conversation, and he eats as she does.

decisions.choice: she wanted the wisdom it would give her
decisions.reason: Readable puts "desirable to make wise" in plain words, keeping the thought that the woman wanted what the serpent promised (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: su marido (L, B); su esposo (R); la mujer / su mujer for the woman and wife (L, B), su esposa (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "mujer" means both "woman" and "wife", as the Hebrew word does, so Literal and Balanced can say "su mujer" and keep the link with "la mujer" (2:23). Readable says "su esposa" and "su esposo", the plainest words for a married couple in all Spanish-speaking countries.

source.text: וַתִּפָּקַ֨חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And were opened [the] eyes of both of them, and they knew that naked they [were], and they sewed leaf[s] of fig and made for themselves loin coverings.

en.L: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they [were] naked, and they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loin coverings.
en.B: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for their waists.
en.R: Then their eyes were opened, and they saw that they had no clothes on. So they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.

es.L: Y se abrieron los ojos de ambos, y supieron que [estaban] desnudos, y cosieron hojas de higuera e hicieron para sí ceñidores.
es.B: Entonces a los dos se les abrieron los ojos y se dieron cuenta de que estaban desnudos. Así que cosieron hojas de higuera y se hicieron con ellas prendas para cubrirse la cintura.
es.R: Entonces se les abrieron los ojos y vieron que no tenían ropa. Así que cosieron hojas de higuera para cubrirse.

fr.L: Et les yeux de tous les deux furent ouverts, et ils surent qu’ils [étaient] nus, et ils cousirent ensemble des feuilles de figuier et se firent des ceintures.
fr.B: Alors leurs yeux à tous les deux s’ouvrirent, et ils se rendirent compte qu’ils étaient nus. Ils cousirent donc des feuilles de figuier pour s’en couvrir la taille.
fr.R: Alors leurs yeux se sont ouverts, et ils ont vu qu’ils n’avaient pas de vêtements. Ils ont donc cousu des feuilles de figuier pour se couvrir.

sw.L: Na macho ya wote wawili yakafunguliwa, nao wakajua kwamba [walikuwa] uchi, wakashona majani ya mtini wakajifanyia vibwebwe.
sw.B: Ndipo macho ya wote wawili yakafunguka, wakatambua kwamba walikuwa uchi. Basi wakashona pamoja majani ya mtini, wakajifanyia mavazi ya kufunga kiunoni.
sw.R: Kisha macho yao yakafunguka, wakaona kwamba hawakuwa na nguo. Basi wakashona majani ya mtini ili kujifunika.

vi.L: Và mắt của cả hai người được mở ra, và họ biết rằng họ [thì] trần truồng, và họ kết lá cây vả lại và làm cho mình những cái khố.
vi.B: Bấy giờ mắt của cả hai người được mở ra, và họ biết mình trần truồng. Vậy họ kết lá cây vả lại và làm thành đồ che quanh hông.
vi.R: Bấy giờ mắt họ được mở ra, và họ thấy mình không mặc quần áo. Vậy họ kết lá cây vả lại để che thân mình.

ko.L: 그리고 그 둘의 눈이 열려, 자기들이 벌거벗은 줄을 알았다. 그리고 무화과나무 잎을 엮어 자기들을 위해 허리 두르개를 만들었다.
ko.B: 그러자 두 사람의 눈이 열려, 자기들이 벌거벗었다는 것을 알게 되었다. 그래서 무화과나무 잎을 엮어 허리를 가리는 것을 만들었다.
ko.R: 그러자 두 사람의 눈이 열렸다. 그들은 자기들이 옷을 입지 않았다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 무화과나무 잎을 엮어 몸을 가렸다.

pt.L: E foram abertos os olhos dos dois, e souberam que eles [estavam] nus, e costuraram folhas de figueira e fizeram para si tangas.
pt.B: Então os olhos dos dois se abriram, e eles perceberam que estavam nus. Por isso costuraram folhas de figueira e fizeram coberturas para a cintura.
pt.R: Então os olhos deles se abriram, e eles viram que estavam sem roupa. Por isso costuraram folhas de figueira para se cobrir.

decisions.choice: their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked: knowledge brings shame
decisions.reason: The serpent's promise comes true in a bitter way: their eyes are opened, and the first thing they know is that they are naked. In 2:25 they were naked and not ashamed; now they hide themselves from each other.

decisions.choice: loin coverings: something tied around the waist
decisions.reason: The word is used for a belt or a garment tied round the waist (2 Samuel 18:11). Their own covering is small and made of leaves; in verse 21 God gives them garments of skin.

decisions.choice: ceñidores
decisions.reason: Something tied around the waist (m2). "Delantales", the traditional word, now means a kitchen apron, and "taparrabos" sounds comic. Balanced describes the thing: "prendas para cubrirse la cintura".

decisions.choice: vibwebwe (L); mavazi ya kufunga kiunoni (B)
decisions.reason: The word is a belt or a garment tied round the waist (m2). "Kibwebwe" is a cloth tied round the waist; Balanced says the same in a phrase, and Readable says only that they covered themselves, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And they heard [the] sound of YHWH God walking about in the garden at [the] breeze of the day, and hid themselves the man and his wife from [the] face of YHWH God among [the] trees of the garden.

en.L: And they heard the sound of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God walking about in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God among the trees of the garden.
en.B: Then they heard the sound of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God walking in the garden at the breezy time of the day, and the man and his wife hid from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God among the trees of the garden.
en.R: In the evening, when the breeze was blowing, they heard {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God walking in the garden. The man and his wife hid from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God among the trees.

es.L: Y oyeron el sonido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} Dios, que se paseaba por el jardín a la brisa del día, y se escondieron el hombre y su mujer de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} Dios entre los árboles del jardín.
es.B: Entonces oyeron el sonido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} Dios, que andaba por el jardín a la hora en que sopla la brisa, y el hombre y su mujer se escondieron {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} Dios entre los árboles del jardín.
es.R: Por la tarde, cuando soplaba la brisa, oyeron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} Dios caminando por el jardín. El hombre y su esposa se escondieron {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} Dios entre los árboles.

fr.L: Et ils entendirent le bruit {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} Dieu qui allait et venait dans le jardin au souffle du jour, et l’homme et sa femme se cachèrent de la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} Dieu au milieu des arbres du jardin.
fr.B: Puis ils entendirent le bruit des pas {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} Dieu qui marchait dans le jardin à l’heure où se lève la brise, et l’homme et sa femme se cachèrent loin {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} Dieu parmi les arbres du jardin.
fr.R: Le soir, quand la brise soufflait, ils ont entendu {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu qui marchait dans le jardin. L’homme et sa femme se sont cachés au milieu des arbres pour que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu ne les voie pas.

sw.L: Na wakasikia sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akitembea-tembea bustanini wakati wa upepo wa mchana, na mtu na mke wake wakajificha mbali na uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu katikati ya miti ya bustani.
sw.B: Kisha wakasikia sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akitembea bustanini wakati upepo wa jioni ulipokuwa ukivuma, na mtu na mke wake wakajificha katikati ya miti ya bustani ili {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu asiwaone.
sw.R: Jioni, upepo ulipokuwa ukivuma, wakamsikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akitembea bustanini. Mtu na mke wake wakajificha kati ya miti ili {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu asiwaone.

vi.L: Và họ nghe tiếng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời đi lại trong vườn lúc gió [thổi] trong ngày, và con người và vợ mình ẩn mình khỏi mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời giữa các cây trong vườn.
vi.B: Bấy giờ họ nghe tiếng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời đi trong vườn vào lúc gió mát trong ngày, và con người cùng vợ mình trốn khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời giữa các cây trong vườn.
vi.R: Buổi chiều, khi gió đang thổi, họ nghe tiếng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời đi trong vườn. Người đàn ông và vợ mình trốn khỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời giữa các cây.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 날의 바람 때에 동산을 거니시는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님의 소리를 들었다. 그리고 그 사람과 그의 아내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님의 얼굴을 피하여 동산의 나무들 사이에 숨었다.
ko.B: 그때 그들은 바람이 불 무렵에 동산을 거니시는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님의 소리를 들었다. 그 사람과 그의 아내는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님을 피하여 동산의 나무들 사이에 숨었다.
ko.R: 저녁이 되어 바람이 불 때, 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 동산을 거니시는 소리를 들었다. 그 사람과 그의 아내는 나무들 사이에 숨어 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님을 피하였다.

pt.L: E ouviram o som {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} Deus andando pelo jardim na brisa do dia, e o homem e a sua mulher se esconderam da face {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} Deus entre as árvores do jardim.
pt.B: Então ouviram o som {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} Deus, que caminhava pelo jardim na hora da brisa do dia, e o homem e a sua mulher se esconderam {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} Deus entre as árvores do jardim.
pt.R: À tardinha, quando a brisa soprava, eles ouviram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus andando pelo jardim. O homem e a sua esposa se esconderam {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} Deus entre as árvores.

decisions.choice: the sound of the LORD God walking
alternatives: the voice of the LORD God
decisions.reason: The word means sound or voice. Here it is the sound of God walking; in verse 10 the man says he heard "your sound".

decisions.choice: walking about in the garden: God is present with them
decisions.reason: The verb, in a form that means walking to and fro, is used later for God's presence among his people in the tabernacle camp (Leviticus 26:12; Deuteronomy 23:14). The story pictures God as near and at home in the garden.

decisions.choice: at the breeze of the day: in the cool of the evening, when the breeze rises
alternatives: in the storm wind of the day
decisions.reason: "The wind of the day" most likely means the time when the breeze comes up, in the afternoon or evening. Some read it as a stormy wind, a sign of God coming in judgment, but there is no other hint of a storm in the scene.

decisions.choice: In the evening, when the breeze was blowing
alternatives: at the breeze of the day
decisions.reason: Readable says what time of day is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: allait et venait ... au souffle du jour (L); marchait ... à l'heure où se lève la brise (B)
alternatives: se promenait ... à la brise du jour
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the to-and-fro sense of the verb form (m2) and "souffle" for the word that means wind or breath; Balanced says what time is meant, when the breeze rises (m3).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And called YHWH God to the man and said to him, where [are] you?

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God called to the man and said to him, "Where [are] you?"
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God called to the man, "Where are you?"
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God called to the man, "Where are you?"

es.L: Y llamó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios al hombre y le dijo: «¿Dónde [estás]?».
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios llamó al hombre: «¿Dónde estás?».
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios llamó al hombre y le preguntó: «¿Dónde estás?».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu appela l’homme et lui dit : « Où [es]-tu ? »
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu appela l’homme : « Où es-tu ? »
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a appelé l’homme : « Où es-tu ? »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwita mtu, akamwambia, "U wapi?"
sw.B: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwita mtu, "Uko wapi?"
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwita mtu, akamwuliza, "Uko wapi?"

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời gọi con người và phán với người: "Ngươi [ở] đâu?"
vi.B: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời gọi con người: "Con ở đâu?"
vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời gọi người đàn ông: "Con đang ở đâu?"

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 그 사람을 부르시며 그에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 어디에 [있느냐]?"
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 그 사람을 부르셨다. "너는 어디에 있느냐?"
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 그 사람을 부르셨다. "너 어디에 있느냐?"

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus chamou o homem e disse a ele: "Onde [estás]?"
pt.B: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus chamou o homem: "Onde estás?"
pt.R: Mas {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus chamou o homem: "Onde estás?"

decisions.choice: where are you: a question that invites the man to come out
decisions.reason: God does not ask because he does not know. The question calls the man to answer and come out of hiding, as later questions (verses 11 and 13; 4:9) give him and the woman the chance to tell the truth.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־קֹלְךָ֥ שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בַּגָּ֑ן וָאִירָ֛א כִּֽי־עֵירֹ֥ם אָנֹ֖כִי וָאֵחָבֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, your sound I heard in the garden, and I was afraid because naked I [was], and I hid myself.

en.L: And he said, "I heard {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sound in the garden, and I was afraid, because I [was] naked, and I hid myself."
en.B: He answered, "I heard {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sound in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid."
en.R: The man answered, "I heard {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the garden, and I was afraid because I was not wearing any clothes. So I hid."

es.L: Y dijo: «Oí {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sonido en el jardín, y tuve miedo, porque [estaba] desnudo, y me escondí».
es.B: Él respondió: «Oí {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} pasos en el jardín, y tuve miedo porque estaba desnudo; por eso me escondí».
es.R: El hombre respondió: «Oí {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} pasos en el jardín y tuve miedo, porque no llevaba ropa. Por eso me escondí».

fr.L: Et il dit : « J’ai entendu {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} bruit dans le jardin, et j’ai pris peur parce que j’[étais] nu, et je me suis caché. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « J’ai entendu le bruit de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} pas dans le jardin, et j’ai eu peur parce que j’étais nu ; alors je me suis caché. »
fr.R: L’homme a répondu : « Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai entendu dans le jardin, et j’ai eu peur parce que je n’avais pas de vêtements. Alors je me suis caché. »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Sauti {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} niliisikia bustanini, nami nikaogopa, kwa kuwa nilikuwa uchi, nikajificha."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Nilisikia vishindo vya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} bustanini, nikaogopa kwa sababu nilikuwa uchi; ndiyo maana nikajificha."
sw.R: Mtu akajibu, "Nilikusikia bustanini, nikaogopa kwa sababu sikuwa na nguo. Basi nikajificha."

vi.L: Và người nói: "Con nghe tiếng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong vườn, và con sợ, vì con [thì] trần truồng, và con đã ẩn mình."
vi.B: Người thưa: "Con nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong vườn, và con sợ vì con trần truồng, nên con trốn."
vi.R: Người đàn ông thưa: "Con nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong vườn, và con sợ vì con không mặc quần áo. Vì vậy con trốn."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "제가 동산에서 주님의 소리를 듣고 두려웠습니다. 제가 벌거벗었기 때문입니다. 그래서 제가 숨었습니다."
ko.B: 그 사람이 대답했다. "동산에서 주님의 소리를 듣고, 제가 벌거벗었으므로 두려워서 숨었습니다."
ko.R: 그 사람이 대답했다. "동산에서 주님의 소리를 들었습니다. 저는 옷을 입지 않아서 무서웠습니다. 그래서 숨었습니다."

pt.L: E ele disse: "Ouvi o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} som no jardim, e tive medo, porque eu [estava] nu, e me escondi."
pt.B: Ele respondeu: "Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ouvi no jardim e fiquei com medo, porque estava nu, e então me escondi."
pt.R: O homem respondeu: "Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ouvi no jardim e fiquei com medo, porque eu estava sem roupa. Por isso me escondi."

decisions.choice: I was afraid because I was naked: fear and shame instead of trust
decisions.reason: The man gives fear and nakedness as his reasons, but not the eating. Their coverings of leaves do not take away his sense of being exposed before God.

decisions.choice: your (lowercase by default; Your with the setting)
decisions.reason: "You" and "your" when someone speaks to God take the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: tus pasos
decisions.reason: The man heard the sound of God walking (verse 8, m1). "Tu voz", the traditional rendering, would suggest that God had spoken, and "tu sonido" is not natural Spanish; "tus pasos" says what he heard. Literal keeps "sonido" to match verse 8.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} (L), {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} (B), {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}} (R)
alternatives: the bare pronouns without a setting
decisions.reason: When someone speaks to God, "tu", "te" and the possessives take the deity pronoun setting, as the English "your" and "you" do (r-en-1). Readable has the elided object "t'" ("je t'ai entendu"), written straight before the verb.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} (L, B); no span in "nilikusikia" (R)
decisions.reason: The free possessive "yako" takes the deity pronoun setting; at Readable the English "you" is the object marker "-ku-" inside the verb, which cannot be capitalised, so it has no span (see 1:5).

decisions.choice: the man says "con" for himself and "Ngài" to God (spanned mid-sentence)
decisions.reason: As the Genesis terms note settles, people speak to God in the forms of prayer: "con" for themselves and "Ngài" for God, with the deity_pronoun setting where the English has one. "thưa" (B, R) marks the man answering God with respect.

decisions.choice: The man speaks to God in 합쇼체, calls himself "저" and God "주님"
decisions.reason: The terms note: people speak to God in the forms of prayer, 합쇼체 with 저 and 주님, and God answers in the plain style with 너. The same holds for the woman in verse 13 and for Cain in chapter 4.

decisions.choice: Eu te ouvi
decisions.reason: "Ouvir o teu som" is not natural Portuguese, and "a tua voz" would make it a voice, where the man heard God walking (m1 of verse 8). Balanced says "Eu te ouvi", as the English Readable does; Literal keeps "o teu som". The man speaks to God with "tu" (style section 4), and the pronoun takes the deity pronoun setting, as in the English.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן־הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, who told you that naked you [were]? From the tree which I commanded you not to eat from it, have you eaten?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Who told you that you [were] naked? Have you eaten from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat?"
en.B: God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?"
en.R: God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat fruit from the tree I told you not to eat from?"

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Quién te dijo que [estabas] desnudo? ¿Del árbol del que te mandé que no comieras, has comido?».
es.B: Dios le preguntó: «¿Quién te dijo que estabas desnudo? ¿Comiste del árbol del que te ordené que no comieras?».
es.R: Dios le preguntó: «¿Quién te dijo que estabas desnudo? ¿Comiste fruta del árbol del que te dije que no comieras?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Qui t’a révélé que tu [étais] nu ? De l’arbre dont je t’avais ordonné de ne pas manger, en as-tu mangé ? »
fr.B: Dieu demanda : « Qui t’a dit que tu étais nu ? Aurais-tu mangé de l’arbre dont je t’avais ordonné de ne pas manger ? »
fr.R: Dieu a demandé : « Qui t’a dit que tu étais nu ? Est-ce que tu as mangé du fruit de l’arbre dont je t’avais dit de ne pas manger ? »

sw.L: Akasema, "Ni nani aliyekuambia kwamba [ulikuwa] uchi? Je, kutoka mti ule niliokuamuru usile kutoka kwake, umekula?"
sw.B: Mungu akauliza, "Nani amekwambia kwamba ulikuwa uchi? Je, umekula kutoka mti ambao nilikuamuru usile?"
sw.R: Mungu akauliza, "Nani alikuambia kwamba ulikuwa uchi? Je, ulikula matunda ya mti ule niliokuambia usile?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Ai đã nói cho ngươi biết rằng ngươi [thì] trần truồng? Có phải ngươi đã ăn [trái] của cây mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho ngươi không được ăn không?"
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời hỏi: "Ai đã nói cho con biết là con trần truồng? Có phải con đã ăn trái của cây mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho con không được ăn không?"
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời hỏi: "Ai đã nói cho con biết là con trần truồng? Có phải con đã ăn trái của cây mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bảo con không được ăn không?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분께서 말씀하셨다. "네가 벌거벗었다고 누가 너에게 알려 주었느냐? 내가 너에게 먹지 말라고 명령한 그 나무에서 네가 먹었느냐?"
ko.B: 하나님께서 물으셨다. "네가 벌거벗었다고 누가 너에게 알려 주었느냐? 내가 먹지 말라고 명령한 그 나무에서 네가 먹었느냐?"
ko.R: 하나님께서 물으셨다. "네가 옷을 입지 않았다고 누가 너에게 말해 주었느냐? 내가 먹지 말라고 한 그 나무의 열매를 네가 먹었느냐?"

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Quem te disse que tu [estavas] nu? Da árvore da qual eu te mandei não comer, dela comeste?"
pt.B: Deus perguntou: "Quem te disse que estavas nu? Por acaso comeste da árvore da qual eu te proibi de comer?"
pt.R: Deus perguntou: "Quem te disse que estavas sem roupa? Comeste a fruta da árvore que eu te disse para não comer?"

decisions.choice: who told you ...? have you eaten ...?: God leads the man to the truth
decisions.reason: The first question shows that the knowledge of nakedness came from somewhere; the second names the tree. God gives the man the chance to confess.

decisions.choice: God asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since the conversation now goes back and forth.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה־לִּ֥י מִן־הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the man, the woman whom you put with me, she gave to me from the tree, and I ate.

en.L: And the man said, "The woman whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put with me, she gave me [fruit] from the tree, and I ate."
en.B: The man said, "The woman {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put here with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it."
en.R: The man said, "It was the woman {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put here with me. She gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it."

es.L: Y dijo el hombre: «La mujer que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pusiste conmigo, ella me dio [fruto] del árbol, y comí».
es.B: El hombre respondió: «La mujer que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pusiste aquí conmigo fue la que me dio fruto del árbol, y comí».
es.R: El hombre dijo: «Fue la mujer que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pusiste aquí conmigo. Ella me dio fruta del árbol, y yo la comí».

fr.L: Et l’homme dit : « La femme que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as mise avec moi, c’est elle qui m’a donné [du fruit] de l’arbre, et j’ai mangé. »
fr.B: L’homme répondit : « La femme que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as placée ici avec moi, c’est elle qui m’a donné du fruit de l’arbre, et j’en ai mangé. »
fr.R: L’homme a dit : « C’est la femme que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as mise ici avec moi. C’est elle qui m’a donné du fruit de l’arbre, et je l’ai mangé. »

sw.L: Na mtu akasema, "Mwanamke yule ambaye {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulimweka pamoja nami, yeye ndiye aliyenipa [tunda] kutoka mti, nami nikala."
sw.B: Mtu akasema, "Ni yule mwanamke {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyemweka hapa pamoja nami; yeye alinipa tunda la mti, nikala."
sw.R: Mtu akasema, "Ni mwanamke yule {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyemweka hapa pamoja nami. Yeye alinipa tunda la mti huo, nami nikalila."

vi.L: Và con người nói: "Người nữ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đặt ở với con, chính nàng đã đưa cho con [trái] của cây ấy, và con đã ăn."
vi.B: Con người thưa: "Người nữ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đặt ở đây với con, chính nàng đã đưa cho con trái của cây ấy, và con đã ăn."
vi.R: Người đàn ông thưa: "Đó là người phụ nữ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đặt ở đây với con. Nàng đã đưa cho con một ít trái của cây ấy, và con đã ăn."

ko.L: 그리고 그 사람이 말했다. "주님께서 저와 함께 있게 하신 여자, 그 여자가 그 나무에서 [열매를] 저에게 주어서 제가 먹었습니다."
ko.B: 그 사람이 말했다. "주님께서 여기 저와 함께 있게 하신 그 여자가 그 나무의 열매를 저에게 주어서, 제가 먹었습니다."
ko.R: 그 사람이 말했다. "주님께서 여기 저와 함께 있게 하신 그 여자 때문입니다. 그 여자가 그 나무의 열매를 저에게 주어서 먹었습니다."

pt.L: E o homem disse: "A mulher que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} puseste comigo, ela me deu [fruto] da árvore, e eu comi."
pt.B: O homem disse: "A mulher que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} colocaste aqui comigo, ela me deu fruto da árvore, e eu comi."
pt.R: O homem disse: "Foi a mulher que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} colocaste aqui comigo. Ela me deu uma fruta da árvore, e eu comi."

decisions.choice: the woman whom you put with me: the man blames the woman, and God
decisions.reason: The man puts the blame first on the woman and then, by "whom you put with me", on God himself. The woman he greeted with joy (2:23) is now "the woman". He admits his own part only at the end: "and I ate".

decisions.choice: [fruit]
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "she gave me from the tree"; Literal brackets the word English needs.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulimweka / uliyemweka
decisions.reason: Swahili adds the free pronoun "wewe" to the verb, which already says "you", to give it the weight the man's words carry: he puts the blame on the woman and on God who gave her (m1). As a free pronoun for God it takes the deity pronoun setting, where the English "you" does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH God to the woman, what [is] this you have done? And said the woman, the serpent deceived me, and I ate.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the woman, "What [is] this you have done?" And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" The woman said, "The serpent tricked me, and I ate."
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the woman, "What have you done?" The woman answered, "The snake tricked me, and I ate the fruit."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios a la mujer: «¿Qué [es] esto que has hecho?». Y dijo la mujer: «La serpiente me engañó, y comí».
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios le dijo a la mujer: «¿Qué es esto que has hecho?». Ella respondió: «La serpiente me engañó, y yo comí».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios le dijo a la mujer: «¿Qué has hecho?». La mujer respondió: «La serpiente me engañó, y comí la fruta».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu dit à la femme : « Qu’est-ce donc que tu as fait ? » Et la femme dit : « Le serpent m’a égarée, et j’ai mangé. »
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu dit à la femme : « Qu’est-ce que tu as fait là ? » La femme dit : « Le serpent m’a dupée, et j’ai mangé. »
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a dit à la femme : « Qu’as-tu fait ? » La femme a répondu : « C’est le serpent qui m’a trompée, et j’ai mangé le fruit. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwambia mwanamke, "Ni jambo gani hili ulilolifanya?" Na mwanamke akasema, "Nyoka alinipotosha, nami nikala."
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwambia mwanamke, "Ni nini hiki ulichofanya?" Mwanamke akasema, "Nyoka alinihadaa, nikala."
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwambia mwanamke, "Umefanya nini?" Mwanamke akajibu, "Nyoka alinidanganya, nikala tunda."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời phán với người nữ: "Điều ngươi đã làm [là] gì vậy?" Và người nữ nói: "Con rắn đã lừa dối con, và con đã ăn."
vi.B: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời phán với người nữ: "Con đã làm gì vậy?" Người nữ thưa: "Con rắn đã lừa con, và con đã ăn."
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời phán với người phụ nữ: "Con đã làm gì vậy?" Người phụ nữ thưa: "Con rắn đã lừa con, và con đã ăn trái ấy."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 여자에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 한 이것이 무엇이냐?" 그리고 여자가 말했다. "뱀이 저를 속여서 제가 먹었습니다."
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 여자에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 어찌하여 이런 일을 하였느냐?" 여자가 대답했다. "뱀이 저를 꾀어서 제가 먹었습니다."
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 여자에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 무슨 일을 저질렀느냐?" 여자가 대답했다. "뱀이 저를 속였습니다. 그래서 제가 열매를 먹었습니다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus disse à mulher: "O que [é] isto que fizeste?" E a mulher disse: "A serpente me iludiu, e eu comi."
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus disse à mulher: "Que foi isso que fizeste?" A mulher disse: "A serpente me ludibriou, e eu comi."
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus disse à mulher: "O que fizeste?" A mulher respondeu: "A cobra me enganou, e eu comi a fruta."

decisions.choice: what is this you have done: a question of reproach
decisions.reason: The question is not a request for information but a rebuke, as when it is put to Abimelech or Laban (12:18; 29:25).

decisions.choice: deceived: led astray by lies
decisions.reason: The verb means to deceive or mislead. Paul uses this verse when he speaks of the serpent's deceit (2 Corinthians 11:3; 1 Timothy 2:14). The woman, like the man, passes on the blame, but what she says is true.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀אֶֽל־הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒ אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה עַל־גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH God to the serpent, because you have done this, cursed [are] you more than all the livestock and more than every animal of the field; on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all [the] days of your life.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed [are] you above all the livestock and above every animal of the field; on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all the days of your life.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all the livestock and all the wild animals! You will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the snake, "Because you did this, you are cursed more than any other animal, tame or wild. You will crawl on your belly, and you will eat dust as long as you live.

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios a la serpiente: «Porque has hecho esto, maldita [eres] por encima de todo el ganado y por encima de todo animal del campo; sobre tu vientre irás, y comerás polvo todos los días de tu vida.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios le dijo a la serpiente: «Por haber hecho esto, eres maldita más que todo el ganado y que todos los animales salvajes. Te arrastrarás sobre tu vientre y comerás polvo todos los días de tu vida.
es.R: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios le dijo a la serpiente: «Por lo que hiciste, eres maldita más que cualquier otro animal, manso o salvaje. Te arrastrarás sobre el vientre y comerás polvo mientras vivas.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu dit au serpent : « Parce que tu as fait cela, tu [es] maudit plus que tout le bétail et plus que tout animal des champs ; sur ton ventre tu iras, et de la poussière tu mangeras tous les jours de ta vie.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu dit au serpent : « Parce que tu as fait cela, tu es maudit plus que tout le bétail et que tous les animaux sauvages ! Tu ramperas sur ton ventre et tu mangeras de la poussière tous les jours de ta vie.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a dit au serpent : « Parce que tu as fait cela, tu es maudit plus que tous les autres animaux, ceux de la ferme comme les animaux sauvages. Tu ramperas sur ton ventre, et tu mangeras de la poussière toute ta vie.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwambia nyoka, "Kwa kuwa umefanya jambo hili, wewe [ni] mlaaniwa kuliko mifugo yote na kuliko kila mnyama wa shambani; utatambaa kwa tumbo lako, na vumbi utakula siku zote za uhai wako.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwambia nyoka, "Kwa sababu umefanya hivi, umelaaniwa kuliko mifugo yote na wanyama wote wa porini! Utatambaa kwa tumbo lako na kula vumbi siku zote za maisha yako.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamwambia nyoka, "Kwa sababu umefanya hivi, umelaaniwa kuliko mnyama mwingine yeyote, wa kufugwa au wa porini. Utatambaa kwa tumbo lako, nawe utakula vumbi muda wote utakaoishi.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời phán với con rắn: "Vì ngươi đã làm điều này, ngươi [bị] nguyền rủa hơn mọi gia súc và hơn mọi thú vật của đồng ruộng; ngươi sẽ đi bằng bụng, và ngươi sẽ ăn bụi đất mọi ngày của đời ngươi.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời phán với con rắn: "Vì ngươi đã làm điều này, ngươi bị nguyền rủa hơn mọi gia súc và mọi thú rừng! Ngươi sẽ bò bằng bụng và ăn bụi đất trọn mọi ngày của đời ngươi.
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời phán với con rắn: "Vì ngươi đã làm điều này, ngươi bị nguyền rủa hơn mọi con vật khác, dù là gia súc hay thú rừng. Ngươi sẽ bò bằng bụng, và ngươi sẽ ăn bụi đất suốt đời ngươi.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 뱀에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 이 일을 하였으니, 너는 모든 가축보다, 들의 모든 짐승보다 더 저주를 받는다. 너는 배로 다니고, 네 평생의 모든 날 동안 흙을 먹을 것이다.
ko.B: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 뱀에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 이런 일을 하였으니, 너는 모든 가축과 모든 들짐승보다 더 저주를 받는다! 너는 평생 동안 배로 기어 다니고 흙을 먹을 것이다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 뱀에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 이런 일을 하였으니, 너는 집짐승이든 들짐승이든 다른 어떤 짐승보다도 더 저주를 받는다. 너는 배로 기어 다니고, 살아 있는 동안 내내 흙을 먹을 것이다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus disse à serpente: "Porque fizeste isto, maldita [és] tu mais que todos os animais domésticos e mais que todo animal do campo; sobre o teu ventre andarás, e pó comerás todos os dias da tua vida.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus disse à serpente: "Por teres feito isso, és amaldiçoada mais do que todos os animais domésticos e todos os animais selvagens! Rastejarás sobre a tua barriga e terás pó para comer enquanto viveres.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus disse à cobra: "Por causa do que fizeste, és amaldiçoada mais do que qualquer outro animal, manso ou selvagem. Vais rastejar de barriga no chão e vais comer poeira a vida toda.

decisions.choice: cursed: placed under God's judgment, cut off from blessing
decisions.reason: To be cursed is the opposite of being blessed (1:22, 28): it means to be under judgment and cut off from good. God curses the serpent and the ground (verse 17), but not the man or the woman.

decisions.choice: on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat: a picture of utter humiliation
alternatives: a description of how snakes came to have no legs
decisions.reason: Crawling and eating dust is a picture of defeat and shame, used of enemies brought low (Psalm 72:9; Isaiah 65:25; Micah 7:17). The verse need not mean that snakes once had legs; it gives the serpent's way of moving a meaning.

decisions.choice: because you have done this: the serpent is not questioned
decisions.reason: God asks the man and the woman to explain themselves, but not the serpent; he pronounces judgment on it at once. The judgments then come in reverse order: serpent, woman, man.

decisions.choice: maudit
decisions.reason: "Maudire", "maudit" render this word throughout the Pentateuch, as the opposite of "bénir" (m1).

decisions.choice: mlaaniwa (L); umelaaniwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kulaani" renders this word throughout the Pentateuch, as the opposite of "kubariki" (m1). Literal uses the noun "mlaaniwa" (one who is cursed), as the Hebrew uses a participle with no verb "to be".

decisions.choice: God calls the serpent "ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: "con" is the word of a father's care, which God uses with the man and the woman; to the serpent under judgment God speaks only with "ngươi". "nguyền rủa" is the word for "curse" through Genesis.

source.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה׀אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And enmity I will put between you and between the woman, and between your offspring and between her offspring; he will strike you [on the] head, and you will strike him [on the] heel.

en.L: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."
en.B: I will make you and the woman enemies, and your offspring and hers. He will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."
en.R: I will make you and the woman enemies. Your children and her children will be enemies too. One of her children will crush your head, and you will bite his heel."

es.L: Y enemistad pondré entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu descendencia y su descendencia; él te herirá la cabeza, y tú le herirás el talón».
es.B: Yo haré que haya enemistad entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu descendencia y la de ella. Él te herirá la cabeza, y tú le herirás el talón».
es.R: Yo haré que la mujer y tú se odien. Tus hijos y los hijos de ella también serán enemigos. Uno de los hijos de ella te va a aplastar la cabeza, y tú le vas a morder el talón».

fr.L: Et je mettrai de l’hostilité entre toi et la femme, et entre ta descendance et sa descendance ; lui te frappera à la tête, et toi, tu le frapperas au talon. »
fr.B: Je ferai de toi et de la femme des ennemis, de ta descendance et de la sienne aussi. Lui te frappera à la tête, et toi, tu le frapperas au talon. »
fr.R: Je ferai de toi et de la femme des ennemis. Tes enfants et ses enfants à elle seront ennemis, eux aussi. L’un de ses enfants à elle t’écrasera la tête, et toi, tu le mordras au talon. »

sw.L: Na uhasama nitauweka kati yako na mwanamke, na kati ya uzao wako na uzao wake; yeye atakupiga kichwani, nawe utampiga kisiginoni."
sw.B: Nitawafanya wewe na mwanamke kuwa maadui, na uzao wako na uzao wake pia. Yeye atakupiga kichwani, nawe utampiga kisiginoni."
sw.R: Nitawafanya wewe na mwanamke kuwa maadui. Watoto wako na watoto wake nao watakuwa maadui. Mmoja wa watoto wake atakuponda kichwa, nawe utamwuma kisigino."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đặt sự thù nghịch giữa ngươi và người nữ, và giữa dòng dõi ngươi và dòng dõi người nữ; người ấy sẽ đánh vào đầu ngươi, và ngươi sẽ đánh vào gót chân người ấy."
vi.B: Ta sẽ làm cho ngươi và người nữ thành kẻ thù của nhau, và dòng dõi ngươi với dòng dõi người nữ cũng vậy. Người ấy sẽ đánh vào đầu ngươi, và ngươi sẽ đánh vào gót chân người ấy."
vi.R: Ta sẽ làm cho ngươi và người phụ nữ thành kẻ thù của nhau. Con cháu ngươi và con cháu người phụ nữ cũng sẽ là kẻ thù của nhau. Một người trong con cháu của người phụ nữ sẽ giày đạp đầu ngươi, và ngươi sẽ cắn gót chân người ấy."

ko.L: 그리고 내가 너와 여자 사이에, 네 씨와 여자의 씨 사이에 원수 됨을 두겠다. 그는 네 머리를 칠 것이고, 너는 그의 발꿈치를 칠 것이다."
ko.B: 내가 너와 여자를 원수가 되게 하고, 네 자손과 여자의 자손도 원수가 되게 하겠다. 그는 네 머리를 치고, 너는 그의 발꿈치를 칠 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 너와 여자를 원수가 되게 하겠다. 네 자손과 여자의 자손도 서로 원수가 될 것이다. 여자의 자손 가운데 하나가 네 머리를 부수고, 너는 그의 발꿈치를 물 것이다."

pt.B: Farei que tu e a mulher sejam inimigas, e também a tua descendência e a dela. Ele golpeará a tua cabeça, e tu golpearás o calcanhar dele."
pt.R: Vou fazer de ti e da mulher inimigas. Os teus descendentes e os descendentes dela também vão ser inimigos. Um dos descendentes dela vai esmagar a tua cabeça, e tu vais morder o calcanhar dele."

decisions.choice: enmity: lasting hostility, as between enemies
decisions.reason: The word is used for deep hostility that leads to violence (Numbers 35:21-22). God himself sets the enmity: the woman and the serpent will not be allies.

decisions.choice: offspring: descendants, either many or one
alternatives: seed (in the sense of a family line)
decisions.reason: The word, literally "seed", can mean a whole line of descendants or a single child (4:25). The first half of the sentence speaks of two lines in conflict; the second narrows to "he" and "you".

decisions.choice: he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel: a struggle in which the serpent receives the deadly blow
alternatives: the ongoing fight between people and snakes, with no further sense
a promise of one descendant of the woman who will defeat the serpent
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for both blows; it means to strike or crush. A blow to the head is deadly; a bite on the heel is painful but not final. The pronoun "he" and his "heel" are singular, and the Septuagint keeps a masculine "he". Jewish and Christian readers have long heard a promise here, and Christians read it as the first announcement of the gospel, fulfilled in Christ's victory over Satan (Romans 16:20; Revelation 12:9). The verse itself speaks of the woman's offspring, without naming one person.

decisions.choice: strike
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses one verb for both blows (m3). Balanced uses one English verb for both, "strike"; Readable says "crush" and "bite" to show what each blow is.

decisions.choice: One of her children
decisions.reason: Readable names the "he" as one of the woman's descendants, which is what the singular pronoun refers to, without deciding who it is (m3).

decisions.choice: descendencia
decisions.reason: The word is literally "seed" and can mean a whole line of descendants or one child (m2). "Simiente" copies the image but is now rare outside older Bibles. "Descendencia" is a singular noun for many people, as the Hebrew is, so the sentence can still narrow to "él"; the plural "descendientes" would lose that.

decisions.choice: herir ... herir
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for both blows (m3). Literal and Balanced use one Spanish verb for both, as English "strike" does; Readable says "aplastar" and "morder" to show what each blow is, as English Readable does. "Le herirás el talón" uses "le" for the person whose heel is struck, as Spanish does with parts of the body.

decisions.choice: lui te frappera ... tu le frapperas
decisions.reason: French "descendance" is feminine, and the traditional French "elle" (or "celle-ci") agrees with it. The Hebrew "he" and "his heel" are masculine and singular (m3), and the sentence narrows from two lines of descendants to one (m2), so French says "lui", which points to one descendant without naming him. One verb, "frapper", serves for both blows, as in the Hebrew (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: uhasama (L); maadui (B, R); yeye atakupiga ... utampiga
decisions.reason: "Uhasama" is deep, lasting hostility (m1). Swahili "yeye" is a person, so it refers to one of the woman's offspring, as the singular Hebrew pronoun does (m3), where a class pronoun agreeing with "uzao" would refer to the line as a whole. One verb, "kupiga", serves for both blows, as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "dòng dõi" (L, B), "con cháu" (R); "người ấy" for "he"
decisions.reason: "dòng dõi" is the word the Genesis terms note settles for offspring, and like the Hebrew it can mean many descendants or one (m2). "người ấy" (that one) keeps the Hebrew "he" without deciding who he is; "nó" would sound like an animal or a child.

The terms note settles "자손" for offspring, with "씨" at Literal where the Hebrew picture of seed matters. Either word can mean one descendant or many (meaning decision m2), which Korean "그는" then narrows to one, as the Hebrew "he" does.

decisions.choice: a descendência
decisions.reason: "Descendência" is the Portuguese word that, like the Hebrew, can mean a whole line of descendants or one of them (m2); "semente" is the image itself but reads as a plant's seed. Literal and Balanced keep the singular "ele" that follows, as the Hebrew does, without deciding who is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: golpeará ... golpearás
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for both blows (m3), so Literal and Balanced use one Portuguese verb for both; Readable says "esmagar" and "morder", as the English Readable says "crush" and "bite".

records.literal_gloss: To the woman he said, increasing I will increase your pain and your pregnancy; in pain you will bear children, and toward your husband [will be] your desire, and he will rule over you.

en.L: To the woman {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I will surely increase your pain and your pregnancy; in pain you will bear children, and your desire [will be] for your husband, and he will rule over you."
en.B: To the woman {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I will greatly increase your pain in childbearing; with pain you will give birth to children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you."
en.R: Then God said to the woman, "I will make having babies very painful for you, and you will give birth in pain. You will long for your husband, and he will rule over you."

es.L: A la mujer dijo: «Ciertamente aumentaré tu dolor y tu embarazo; con dolor darás a luz hijos, y hacia tu marido [será] tu deseo, y él te dominará».
es.B: A la mujer le dijo: «Haré mucho más intensos tus dolores de parto; con dolor traerás hijos al mundo. Tu deseo se dirigirá a tu marido, y él te dominará».
es.R: Luego Dios le dijo a la mujer: «Haré que tener hijos te cause mucho dolor; darás a luz con dolor. Tu deseo te llevará hacia tu esposo, y él te dominará».

fr.L: À la femme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je multiplierai, oui, je multiplierai ta peine et ta grossesse ; dans la peine tu mettras au monde des enfants, et vers ton mari [sera] ton désir, et lui dominera sur toi. »
fr.B: À la femme, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je rendrai très grandes tes souffrances quand tu porteras un enfant ; c’est dans la douleur que tu mettras au monde des enfants. Ton désir te portera vers ton mari, et lui dominera sur toi. »
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit à la femme : « Je vais rendre la naissance des bébés très douloureuse pour toi, et tu accoucheras dans la douleur. Tu seras attirée vers ton mari, et il dominera sur toi. »

sw.L: Kwa mwanamke akasema, "Kuzidisha nitazidisha maumivu yako na mimba yako; kwa maumivu utazaa watoto, na kuelekea mume wako [itakuwa] shauku yako, naye atatawala juu yako."
sw.B: Kwa mwanamke akasema, "Nitaongeza sana maumivu yako wakati wa kuzaa; kwa maumivu utazaa watoto. Shauku yako itakuwa kwa mume wako, naye atatawala juu yako."
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akamwambia mwanamke, "Nitafanya kuzaa watoto kuwe na maumivu makali kwako, nawe utajifungua kwa maumivu. Utamtamani mume wako, naye atakutawala."

vi.L: Với người nữ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chắc chắn sẽ làm gia tăng sự đau đớn của ngươi và sự mang thai của ngươi; trong đau đớn ngươi sẽ sinh con cái, và sự ao ước của ngươi [sẽ hướng về] chồng ngươi, và người sẽ cai trị ngươi."
vi.B: Với người nữ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho sự đau đớn của con khi mang thai sinh nở gia tăng rất nhiều; con sẽ sinh con cái trong đau đớn. Con sẽ ao ước chồng mình, và người sẽ cai trị con."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Chúa Trời phán với người phụ nữ: "{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho việc mang thai sinh con của con rất đau đớn, và con sẽ sinh con trong đau đớn. Con sẽ khao khát chồng mình, và người sẽ cai trị con."

ko.L: 여자에게는 말씀하셨다. "내가 네 고통과 네 임신을 크게 더하겠다. 너는 고통 속에서 자식을 낳을 것이다. 그리고 네 갈망은 네 남편을 향할 것이고, 그는 너를 다스릴 것이다."
ko.B: 여자에게는 이렇게 말씀하셨다. "내가 너에게 아이를 배는 고통을 크게 더하겠다. 너는 고통 속에서 자식을 낳을 것이다. 너는 남편을 갈망하고, 남편은 너를 다스릴 것이다."
ko.R: 하나님께서 여자에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 너에게 아기 낳는 일을 아주 고통스럽게 하겠다. 너는 아파하며 아기를 낳을 것이다. 너는 남편을 몹시 바라고, 남편은 너를 다스릴 것이다."

pt.L: À mulher {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Certamente multiplicarei a tua dor e a tua gravidez; com dor darás à luz filhos, e para o teu marido [será] o teu desejo, e ele te dominará."
pt.B: À mulher {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Aumentarei muito as dores da tua gravidez; com dor terás os teus filhos. O teu desejo se voltará para o teu marido, e ele te dominará."
pt.R: Então Deus disse à mulher: "Vou fazer com que ter filhos seja muito doloroso para ti, e darás à luz com dor. Vais ansiar pelo teu marido, e ele vai te dominar."

decisions.choice: your pain and your pregnancy: the pain of pregnancy and childbirth
decisions.reason: Two nouns joined by "and" often express one idea in Hebrew. The next line makes clear that the pain of bearing children is meant. The word for pain is the same as the man's "painful toil" in verse 17: both now carry out their callings (1:28) in pain.

decisions.choice: your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you: a relationship bent by the fall
alternatives: your desire will be to control your husband, but he will rule over you
your longing for your husband will lead to his ruling over you
decisions.reason: The word for desire is used only twice more: of a man's love for a woman (Song of Songs 7:10) and of sin's desire to master Cain, which he must rule over (4:7). Read with 4:7, it is a desire to control; read with the Song, it is longing. Either way, the verse describes a relationship spoiled by sin, with rule where there had been partnership (2:18-24). It describes what will happen, not what God commands.

decisions.choice: pain in childbearing (B); having babies very painful (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two nouns into one idea (m1); Literal keeps both.

decisions.choice: ta peine ... dans la peine (L); souffrances, douleur (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for pain here is related to the man's "painful toil" in verse 17 (m1). Literal says "peine" in both verses, a word that covers both suffering and hard labour, so that the link can be seen; Balanced and Readable say "douleur", the word for the pain of childbirth. "Multiplier" is doubled at Literal, as the Hebrew doubles the verb.

decisions.choice: shauku (L, B); utamtamani (R)
decisions.reason: "Tamaa" often means craving or lust; "shauku" is a strong longing, which leaves open both readings of the word, longing or a desire to control (m2).

decisions.choice: dominará
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the lights in 1:16-18, there rendered "governar"; here it describes a relationship bent by the fall (m2), and Portuguese "dominar" says that, where "governar" would sound like an office. Cain is told to "dominar" sin with the same verb in 4:7.
